questions.q: For a periodic motion represented by the equation $y = sin \omegat + cos \omegat$ the amplitude of the motion is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given the equation of motion is

$y = sin \omegat + cos \omegat . . . \left(1\right)$

Simplify equation (1) to obtain the standard form:

\begin{cases}$y & = & $\sqrt{2} \left($sin\omegatcos\dfrac{π}{4} +cos\omegatsin\dfrac{π}{4}\right)\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \sqrt{2}sin\left(\omegat + $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Comparing equation (2) with standard equation of~SHM~$y = Asin \left(\omegat + ϕ\right)$, we get amplitude of the given oscillation as~\sqrt{2}.

$

questions.q: A simple pendulum oscillating in air has period $T$ . The bob of the pendulum is completely immersed in a non-viscous liquid. The density of the liquid is $\dfrac{1}{16}th$ of the material of the bob. If the bob is inside liquid all the time, its period of oscillation in this liquid is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the density of bob is $\sigma$ & density of liquid is $\dfrac{\sigma}{16}$ .
Now, Net downward force on bob = Weight - Buoyancy
$= \sigmaVg - \dfrac{\sigma}{16}Vg = \dfrac{15}{16}\sigmaVg$
Net effective gravitational acceleration $= \dfrac{\dfrac{15}{16}\sigmaVg}{\sigmaV} = \dfrac{15}{16}g$
Time period \left(T\right) = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{geff}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{\dfrac{15}{16}g}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{16}{15}\dfrac{l}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{15}} ∙ \left(2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}\right) = \dfrac{4}{15}T$
$= 4T\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{15}}

questions.q: When a particle of mass& $m$~is attached to a vertical spring of spring constant~$k$~and released, its motion, is described by~$y\left(t\right) = {y}_{0}\sin^{2}\omega t$, where '$y$' is measured from the lower end of upstretched spring. Then~$\omega$& is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$y = {y}_{0}\sin^{2}\omega t$

$y = \dfrac{y0}{2} ( 1 - cot2\omega t )$

$y - \dfrac{y0}{2} = - \dfrac{y0}{2}cos2\omega t$

$Y = Acos2\omega t$

$2\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

maximum displacemnet~$= {y}_{0} = \dfrac{mg}{k}$

${y}_{0} \times ( 2\omega{)}^{2} = 2g$

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{2{y}_{0}}}$

questions.q: The equation of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is given by $x = sin\pi\left(t + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)m$. At $t = 1s$, the speed of particle will be (Given: $\pi = 3 . 14$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,& $x = sin \left(\pit + \dfrac{π}{3}\right)

Velocity $v = $\dfrac{d x}{d t} = \picos \left(\pit + $\dfrac{π}{3}\right)$

Now, at~$t = 1s$,~$v = \picos \left(\pi + $\dfrac{π}{3}\right)

~$v = $\dfrac{- \pi}{2} = \dfrac{- 3 . 14}{2} = -$1 . 57ms^{- 1} ⇒ \left|v\right| = 157cms^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: A simple pendulum of length $1 \mathrm{~m}$ is oscillating with an angular frequency $10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$. The support of the pendulum starts oscillating up and down with a small angular frequency of $1 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ and an amplitude of $10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}$. The relative change in the angular frequency of the pendulum is best given by :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Angular frequency of pendulum $\omega=\sqrt{\frac{g}{\ell}}\therefore$ relative change in angular frequency $\frac{\Delta \omega}{\omega}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{\Delta \mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{g}}[$ as length remains constant $]\Delta g=2 \mathrm{~A} \omega_s^{2}\left[\omega_{s}=\right.$ angular frequency of support and, $\mathrm{A}=$ amplitude] $\frac{\Delta \omega}{\omega}=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2 \mathrm{~A} \omega_{\mathrm{S}}^{2}}{\mathrm{~g}}\Delta \omega=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2 \times 1^{2} \times 10^{-2}}{10}=10^{-3} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm\sec$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement $I$: A second's pendulum has a time period of $1$ second.

Statement $II$: It takes precisely one second to move between the two extreme positions. In the light of the above statements,

choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement& $I$ is false but Statement~$II$ is true
Both Statement& $I$ and Statement~$II$ are true
Both Statement& $I$ and Statement~$II$ are False
Statement& $I$ is true but Statement $II$& is false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Second pendulum has a time period of $2s$ so statement~$1$ is false but from one extreme to other it takes only half the time period so statement $2$ is true.

questions.q: A particle executes S.H.M., the graph of velocity as a function of displacement is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$v^{2} = {ω}^{2} \left(A^{2} - x^{2}\right)$

\dfrac{v2}{\omega2} +$x^{2} = A^{2}$
\dfrac{v2}{\left(\omegaA\right)2} + \dfrac{x2}{A2} =$1

This is an equation of an ellipse.

$

questions.q:
For a body executing S.H.M. :
(a) Potential energy is always equal to its& $K . E .$
(b) Average potential and kinetic energy over any given time interval are always equal.
(c) Sum of the kinetic and potential energy at any point of time is constant.
(d) Average~$K . E .$& in one time period is equal to average potential energy in one time period.
Choose the most appropriate option from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The formula of kinetic energy in S.H.M. is,& $K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}m{ω}^{2}\left(\sqrt{A^{2} - x^{2}}\right)2$, where~$A$~is the amplitude of the S.H.M. the formula of potential energy is,~$P . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}m{ω}^{2}x^{2}$, so the net energy is defined as,~$T . E . = P . E . + K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}m{ω}^{2}A^{2}$~so the total energy is always constant. Since, energy changes from potential to kinetic and vice-versa the average~$K . E .$~in one time period~is equal to the average~$P . E .$& in one time period.

questions.q:
Two blocks of masses $m$ and $M,(M \gt m)$, are placed on a frictionless table as shown in figure. A massless spring with spring constant k is attached with the lower block. If the system is slightly displaced and released then
($\mu=$ coefficient of friction between the two blocks)

(A) The time period of small oscillation of the two blocks is $\mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{(\mathrm{~m}+\mathrm{M})}{\mathrm{k}}}$
(B) The acceleration of the blocks is $\mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{kx}}{\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}}$ ($\mathrm{x}=$ displacement of the blocks from the mean position)
(C) The magnitude of the frictional force on the upper block is $\frac{m \mu|x|}{M+m}$
(D) The maximum amplitude of the upper block, if it does not slip, is $\frac{\mu(M+m) g}{k}$
(E) Maximum frictional force can be $\mu(\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}) \mathrm{g}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) As both blocks moving together so Time period $=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{~m}}{\mathrm{~K}}} ;$ where $\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}$
$\mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{~K}}}$
(B) Let block is displaced by x in $(+\mathrm{ve})$ direction so force on block will be in(-ve) direction
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{F}=-\mathrm{Kx} \\ & (\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}) \mathrm{a}=-\mathrm{Kx} \\ & \mathrm{a}=-\frac{\mathrm{Kx}}{(\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m})}
\end{aligned}$
(C) As upper block is moving due to friction thus
$\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{ma}=\frac{\mathrm{mKx}}{(\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m})}$
(D) This option is like two block problem in friction for maximum amplitude, force on block is also maximum, for which both blocks are moving together.

$\begin{aligned}
& K A=(M+m) a \\ & a=\frac{K A}{(M+m)} \\ & f=m a=\frac{m K A}{(M+m)} \\ & f_{\max }=f_L=\mu \mathrm{mg} \\ & f=\mu m g \\ & \frac{m K A}{(M+m)}=\mu m g \\ & A=\frac{\mu(M+m) g}{K}
\end{aligned}$
(E) Maximum friction can be $\mu \mathrm{mg}$ as force is acting between blocks \& normal force here is mg.

questions.q: For a simple harmonic motion in a mass spring system shown, the surface is frictionless. When the mass of the block is $1$ kg, the angular frequency is ${ω}_{1}$. When the mass block is $2$ kg the angular frequency is ${ω}_{2}$. The ratio $\dfrac{\omega2}{\omega1}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In case of SHM in spring-block system, angular frequency is given by,& $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$.

Therefore,

$\dfrac{\omega2}{\omega1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m1}{m2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion (SHM). The ratio of potential energy and kinetic energy of the particle when its displacement is half of its amplitude will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the potential energy of the particle executing SHM is given by

$P = \dfrac{1}{2}m{ω}^{2}x^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the kinetic energy of the same particle is given by

$K = $\dfrac{1}{2}$m{ω}^{2} \left(A^{2} - x^{2}\right) . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (1) by equation (2) to obtain the required ratio.

\begin{cases}\dfrac{P}{K}$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}m{ω}^{2}x^{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}m{ω}^{2}\left(A^{2} - x^{2}\right)}$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{x2}{A^{2} - x^{2}} . . . \left($3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute~\dfrac{A}{2}~for~$x$~into equation (3) to calculate the required ratio.

\begin{cases}\dfrac{P}{K}$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)2}{A^{2} - \left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)2}$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{1}{3}\end{cases}

questions.q: The displacement of simple harmonic oscillator after $3$& seconds starting from its mean position is equal to half of its amplitude. The time period of harmonic motion is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Displacement equation is given by& $x = Asin\omegat$

Now, when amplitude is halved, $\dfrac{A}{2} = Asin\omegat$

Or~$\omegat = \dfrac{π}{6}$

At,~$t = 3s$,~$\omega\left(3\right) = \dfrac{π}{6}⇒ \omega = \dfrac{π}{18}$

Time period,~$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{ω} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\dfrac{π}{18}} = 36s$

questions.q: $The amplitude of a mass-spring system, which is executing simple harmonic motion decreases with time. If mass& $= 500g$, Decay constant $= 20gs^{- 1}$ then how much time is required for the amplitude of the system to drop to half of its initial value?  \left(ln2 = 0 . 693\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$A = {A}_{0}e^{- \gammat} = {A}_{0}e^{- \dfrac{bt}{2m}}$

$\dfrac{A0}{2} = {A}_{0}e^{- \dfrac{bt}{2m}}$

$\dfrac{bt}{2m} = ln2$

$t = \dfrac{2m}{b}ln2 = \dfrac{2 \times 500 \times 0 . 693}{20}$

$t = 34 . 65$ second.

questions.q: A particle undergoing simple harmonic motion has time dependent displacement given by $x(t)=\mathrm{A} \sin \frac{\pi t}{90}$. The ratio of kinetic to potential energy of this particle at $\mathrm{t}=210 \mathrm{~s}$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Kinetic energy, $\mathrm{k}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m} \omega^{2} \mathrm{~A}^{2} \cos ^{2} \omega \mathrm{t}$ Potential energy, $U=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^{2} A^{2} \sin ^{2} \omega t\frac{k}{U}=\cot ^{2} \omega t=\cot ^{2} \frac{\pi}{90}(210)=\frac{1}{3}$

questions.q:
In a linear Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM)

(A) Restoring force is directly proportional to the displacement.

(B) The acceleration and displacement are opposite in direction.

(C) The velocity is maximum at mean position.

(D) The acceleration is minimum at extreme points.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The equations of SHM is given by

$F = – kx$

$⇒ a = – {ω}^{2}x$

Velocity is given by,~$v = \omega\sqrt{A^{2} - x^{2}}$.

Clearly, velocity is maximum at mean position and acceleration is maximum at extreme positions.

Hence, this is the correct option.

questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of $5$ cm . When the particle is at $4$ cm from the mean position, the magnitude of its velocity in $SI$ units is equal to that of its acceleration. Then, its periodic time in seconds is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$v = \omega\sqrt{{5}^{2} - {4}^{2}} = 3\omega$

$a = {\omega}^{2} \times 4$

\left|a\right| = \left|v\right|$

$4{\omega}^{2} = 3\omega$

$\omega = \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$

$T = \dfrac{8\pi}{3}sec

questions.q: Two identical springs of spring constant $2k$ are attached to a block of mass $m$ and to fixed support (see figure). When the mass is displaced from equilibrium position on either side, it executes simple harmonic motion. The time period of oscillations of this system is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For parallel combination& ${k}_{eq} = {k}_{1} + {k}_{2}$

${k}_{eq} = 4k$

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{keq}} ⇒ T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{4k}} ⇒ T = \pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$

questions.q: A particle is doing simple harmonic motion of amplitude $0.06 \mathrm{~m}$ and time period $3.14 \mathrm{~s}$. The maximum velocity of the particle is _______ $\mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{V}_{\max } & =\omega \mathrm{A} \quad \text { at mean position } \\
& =\frac{2 \pi}{\mathrm{T}} \mathrm{A}=\frac{2 \pi}{\pi} \times 0.06=0.12 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm\sec \\
\mathrm{V}_{\max } & =12 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm\sec
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The metallic bob of simple pendulum has the relative density $5$. The time period of this pendulum is $10s$. If the metallic bob is immersed in water, then the new time period becomes $5\sqrt{x}s$. The value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the bob is immersed in water its effective weight& is& $mg^{'} = mg - {F}_{B}$, where,~${F}_{B}$~is buoyant force.

Then,~$g^{'} = \dfrac{mg - {F}_{B}}{m}$~$= \dfrac{{ρ}_{B}Vg - {ρ}_{W}Vg}{{ρ}_{B}V}$

$= \left(\dfrac{{ρ}_{B} - {ρ}_{w}}{ρB}\right)g$~$= \dfrac{5 - 1}{5} \times g= \dfrac{4}{5}g$

Now, time period of simple pendulum is given by~$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$

Thus, the ratio~$\dfrac{T '}{T} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{g '}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{\dfrac{4}{5}g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{4}}$

$⇒ T^{'} = T\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{4}} = \dfrac{10}{2}\sqrt{5}$

Thus, the new time period is~$T^{'} = 5\sqrt{5}s$.~

Hence, value of~$x = 5$.

questions.q: A particle of mass $1$ kg is hanging from a spring of force constant $100Nm^{- 1} .$~The mass is pulled slightly downward and released so that it executes free simple harmonic motion with time period $T .$~The time when the kinetic energy and potential energy of the system will~become equal, is $\dfrac{T}{n} .$ The value of $n$ is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$KE = PE$
$\dfrac{1}{2}k\left(A^{2} - x^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2}$
$x^{2} = \dfrac{A2}{2}$
$x = \pm \dfrac{A}{2}$
$y = Asin\omegat$

$\dfrac{A}{2} = Asin\omegat$
$sin\dfrac{π}{4} = sin\omegat$
$\omegat = \dfrac{π}{4}; t = \dfrac{T}{8} .$ Thus $n = 8$

questions.q: In the figure given below. a block of mass $M = 490g$~placed on a frictionless table is connected with two springs having same spring constant ($K = 2Nm^{- 1}$). If the block is horizontally displaced through $X$~$m$ then the number of complete oscillations it will make in $14\pi$ seconds will be ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Both the springs are connected in parallel, therefore

${K}_{eq} = K + K = 2K$

Now, time period of spring-block system is given by,

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{Keq}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2K}}$

Given here,~$m = 490gm= 0 . 49kg$~and~$K = 2Nm^{- 1}$

So,~$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{0 . 49}{2 \times 2}}$

$= 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{49}{400}} = 2\pi\dfrac{7}{20} = \dfrac{7\pi}{10}$

Now, number of oscillation in $14\pi$ is

$N = \dfrac{time}{T} = \dfrac{14\pi}{\dfrac{7\pi}{10}} = 20$

questions.q: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude $A$. Its speed is increased to three times at an instant when its displacement is $\dfrac{2A}{3}$. The new amplitude of motion is $\dfrac{nA}{3}$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Speed in SHM in terms of displacement is given by, $v = \omega\sqrt{A^{2} - x^{2}}$.

at $x = \dfrac{2A}{3}$, we get

$v = \omega\sqrt{A^{2} - \left(\dfrac{2A}{3}\right)2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}A\omega}{3}$

Let the new amplitude be$= A '$

Then,

$v ' = 3v ⇒ \omega\sqrt{\left(A '\right)2 - \left(\dfrac{2A}{3}\right)2} = \sqrt{5}A\omega$

$⇒ A ' = \dfrac{7}{3}A$

Therefore, $n = 7$.
